headline: Kimi Code CLI is Moonshot AI's open-source terminal coding agent
summary: This AI coding agent operates directly in your terminal, reading and editing code, running shell commands, and executing tasks step-by-step. It's compatible with Moonshot AI, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google models.
details: Kimi Code CLI is Moonshot AI's open-source terminal-based AI coding agent, designed to streamline development workflows. It allows developers to describe tasks in plain language, and the agent then reads and edits code, runs shell commands, and processes tasks step-by-step based on the results.

The agent plans its steps, modifies code, runs tests, and reports its actions, all within the terminal environment. It features a fast single-binary install, a clean TUI (Text User Interface), subagents for specialized tasks, and support for the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) for editor integration.

Kimi Code CLI works out-of-the-box with Moonshot AI's Kimi models. It can also be configured to use other compatible providers like Anthropic, OpenAI, or Google by editing a simple config file. The project is written in TypeScript, distributed as a single binary, and is MIT licensed.

Installation is straightforward via an official install script or npm. For Windows users, Git for Windows is required as Kimi Code CLI utilizes its bundled Git Bash as the shell environment. The install script downloads the latest release, verifies its checksum, and adds the executable to your PATH.

Once installed and logged in, users can simply describe their desired task in plain English. The agent automatically uses file-reading and search tools to gather context. Read-only operations proceed without confirmation, while any actions that modify files or run shell commands require user approval.

Advanced features include support for the Agent Client Protocol (ACP), enabling direct session control from editors like Zed and JetBrains. This integration reuses existing CLI credentials, eliminating the need for separate logins within the editor.

Configuration files, session records, logs, and update caches are stored by default under ~/.kimi-code/. This path can be customized by setting the KIMI_CODE_HOME environment variable. Uninstallation is as simple as deleting the executable for script installs or using `npm uninstall`.

headline_marked: [[Thread-based circuits]] track health from inside your clothes, no rigid gadgets needed
headline: Thread-based circuits track health from inside your clothes, no rigid gadgets needed
summary: Researchers at Tufts University have developed working circuits directly on textile threads, enabling health monitoring from within clothing without rigid devices. These flexible circuits can bend, twist, and stretch while remaining functional.
details: Researchers at Tufts University have developed working circuits directly onto textile threads, enabling health monitoring from within clothing. These innovative threads can track vital signs like breathing patterns and blinking, behaving more like fabric than traditional electronics.

Unlike conventional flat circuit boards, these circuits integrate transistors, resistors, sensors, and amplifiers onto a single strand of thread. This design allows the circuit to bend, twist, coil, and stretch without losing functionality, making it truly wearable.

The technology uses a gold-coated thread with tiny, flexible organic transistors attached directly. Conductive polymer coatings form electrical pathways and passive components, while a soft eutectogel acts as the transistor's gate dielectric.

A key feature of the eutectogel is its self-healing capability; torn sections can be rejoined with gentle heat, restoring both mechanical strength and electrical performance. Unlike other hydrogels, eutectogels also resist drying out.

While manufacturing gold thread circuits isn't a home project, the concept makes sewable electronics approachable for educational purposes. Enthusiasts can start with LilyPad-style boards and conductive thread to prototype their own breathing sensors.
